original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descending-types-morphisms}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base.
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, fppf, \etale, smooth, syntomic\}$.
Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is stable under any base change
(see Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-preserved-by-base-change}),
\item if $Y_j \to V_j$, $j = 1, \ldots, m$ have $\mathcal{P}$,
then so does $\coprod Y_j \to \coprod V_j$, and
\item for any surjective morphism of affines
$X \to S$ which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
any descent datum $(V, \varphi)$ relative
to $X$ over $S$ such that $\mathcal{P}$ holds for
$V \to X$ is effective.
\end{enumerate}
Then morphisms of type $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy descent for $\tau$-coverings.
statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ be a property of morphisms of schemes over a base, and let $\tau\in\{\mathrm{fpqc},\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic}\}$. Say that *morphisms of type $\mathcal P$ satisfy descent for $\tau$-coverings* if, for every $\tau$-covering $\{U_i\to S\}$, every scheme descent datum $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ with each $X_i\to U_i$ having $\mathcal P$ is effective, i.e. isomorphic to the canonical pullback descent datum of some $S$-scheme.

Suppose (1) $\mathcal P$ is preserved by arbitrary base change; (2) $\mathcal P$ is preserved by finite disjoint unions of morphisms, so that if $Y_j\to V_j$ have $\mathcal P$ for $1\leq j\leq m$, then $\coprod_jY_j\to\coprod_jV_j$ has $\mathcal P$; and (3) for each surjective map of affine schemes $X\to S$ of the corresponding class—flat for fpqc, flat and of finite presentation for fppf, étale for étale, smooth for smooth, and syntomic for syntomic—every descent datum $(V,\varphi)$ for $X/S$ with $V\to X$ having $\mathcal P$ is effective. Then morphisms of type $\mathcal P$ satisfy descent for all $\tau$-coverings. This asserts effectivity of the descent datum; the definition does not separately assert that its descended morphism has $\mathcal P$.
hypotheses: P is base-change stable, finite-coproduct stable, and affine-singleton descent effective for the indicated τ-coverings.
conclusions: Every τ descent datum of P-type schemes is effective.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is affine, then the descent datum is
effective.
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. If $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering of $S$ and each $X_i\to S_i$ is an affine morphism, then the datum is effective: there is an $S$-scheme $X$ and compatible isomorphisms $X\times_SS_i\simeq X_i$. In fact one may construct $X$ by faithfully flat descent of the quasi-coherent algebras defining the affine morphisms.
hypotheses: fpqc cover and a scheme descent datum whose local structure maps are affine.

Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-quasi-affine}
Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\{X_i \to S\}_{i\in I}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Let $(V_i/X_i, \varphi_{ij})$ be a descent datum
relative to $\{X_i \to S\}$. If each morphism
$V_i \to X_i$ is quasi-affine, then the descent datum is
effective.
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal U=\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ a family of morphisms, and $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ a descent datum for schemes relative to $\mathcal U$: each $X_i$ is an $S_i$-scheme, and $\varphi_{ij}:X_i\times_S S_j\overset{\sim}{\to} S_i\times_S X_j$ is an isomorphism over $S_i\times_S S_j$, satisfying the usual cocycle condition on triple overlaps. Such a datum is *effective* if it is isomorphic to the canonical descent datum $(S_i\times_S X,\mathrm{can})$ arising from some $S$-scheme $X$. Assume $\mathcal U$ is an fpqc covering and each $X_i\to S_i$ is quasi-affine, meaning that locally on the base the source is quasi-compact and an open subscheme of an affine scheme over that base. Then the descent datum $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ is effective. In particular, the relative affine hulls $\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_{S_i}((p_i)_*\mathcal O_{X_i})$ descend by affine descent, and the compatible quasi-compact open subschemes $X_i$ descend to an open subscheme of the resulting affine hull over $S$.
hypotheses: fpqc cover and a scheme descent datum whose local structure maps are quasi-affine.

statement:
Fix $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic}\}$ (explicitly *not* fpqc), and a big $\tau$-site $\operatorname{Sch}_{\tau}$ containing a scheme $S$. Let $\{S_i\to S\}_{i\in I}$ be a covering in $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$. For an object $T$ of the site, write $h_T$ for its representable sheaf $U\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_S(U,T)$; representable presheaves are sheaves for these topologies.

There is an equivalence between (a) the category of scheme descent data $(X_i,\varphi_{ij})$ for this covering, with each $X_i$ an object of $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$, and (b) the category of sheaves of sets $F$ on $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for which the fibre products $h_{S_i}\times F$ (over $h_S$, the terminal sheaf) are representable for every $i$. Under the equivalence, $X_i$ represents $h_{S_i}\times F$, and the overlap isomorphisms correspond to the canonical identification of both pullbacks with $h_{S_i}\times h_{S_j}\times F$. Conversely, $F$ is obtained by gluing the sheaves $h_{X_i}$ along these identifications, equivalently as their sheaf coequalizer. Moreover, $F$ itself is representable if and only if the corresponding descent datum is effective.
hypotheses: τ is one of Zariski/fppf/étale/smooth/syntomic but not fpqc; big τ site, S object, τ-covering {S_i→S}.
conclusions: Scheme descent data with the indicated objects are equivalent to sheaves locally representable on the cover; global representability is equivalent to effectivity.
